public_headline: Pilot Reports Erratic White Lights at 39,000 Feet Over South Carolina
public_tldr: An FAA incident report from August 2023 documents a commercial pilot observing an unorganised group of white lights moving erratically near their altitude while flying from Florida to New Jersey. The report contains no follow-up investigation, no radar corroboration, and no explanation for what was observed.
public_narrative:
On 28 August 2023, the pilot of an Embraer E35L business jet (registration N224LD) flying from Opa-locka, Florida, to Teterboro, New Jersey, reported an unidentified aerial phenomenon to Jacksonville Air Route Traffic Control Centre (ARTCC). The aircraft was heading north at flight level 390 — roughly 39,000 feet.

The pilot described seeing an unorganised group of white lights on the left side of the aircraft, moving erratically between flight levels 390 and 410 (approximately 39,000 to 41,000 feet). The sighting occurred in the vicinity of Florence, South Carolina. No evasive action was taken, and no law enforcement was notified.

The document is a standard FAA Washington Operations Center incident report — a preliminary record of what a pilot called in, not an investigation. It contains no radar data, no additional witness accounts, and no follow-up analysis. The FAA recorded the report and that appears to be where this particular record ends.

There is little evidence of redaction in this document. What it lacks is not hidden — it simply was never gathered. This is a single pilot's visual observation at night, logged through routine FAA channels.
public_caveats: This is a single-source pilot report with no corroborating radar data or independent witness accounts included in the record.
The description of 'unorganised white lights moving erratically' is a subjective visual observation made at night — it has not been verified by instruments.
This is a preliminary incident log, not an investigation. No follow-up findings or conclusions are documented.
The FAA logged the report through its standard operations centre process. There is no indication the phenomenon was identified or explained.
Coordinates in the metadata place the sighting near Florence, South Carolina, but the location field in the original record is not explicitly stated in the document text.
